message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I have $847 and three unmortgaged properties. I am on Vermont Avenue. Player 1 has $137 and several monopolies. I need to decide what to do next.

Player 2 has a dark blue monopoly with three houses on both Boardwalk and Park Place. Rent there would bankrupt me. I need to avoid that.

Player 4 owns a light blue monopoly and two railroads. I need Virginia Avenue to complete the pink monopoly with St. Charles Place and States Avenue. I will not sell my pink properties or Baltic Avenue.

I am weighing trade options. Player 4 wants Marvin Gardens for a yellow monopoly, but I do not have it. I could try to acquire something useful from them.

Player 1 has no urgent needs from me, and I should not give away cash. Player 2 is too dangerous to trade with; giving them money would let them build more houses on their dark blue monopoly. I am now considering whether any trade could actually help me complete a monopoly.

I cannot trade for Virginia Avenue because it is unowned. Player 4 will not break up their light blue monopoly. I am now looking for a trade that could block another player or complete a valuable set.

Player 2 can buy one more house on either dark blue property. That would raise rent to $1300 or $1700, which would bankrupt me even with my current cash. Mortgaging all three properties would only yield about $170, so that is not enough to survive.

Mortgaging all three properties would only raise about $170, bringing total cash to roughly $1017. That is still short of the $1100 rent on Park Place and far below the $1400 on Boardwalk. I cannot trade to raise more money mid-rent, so mortgaging now will not prevent bankruptcy if I land on dark blue.

Mortgaging now would trap me in a losing position. I would need to pay 10% interest to unmortgage properties later, and selling everything for cash would leave me with no path to a monopoly. The only viable strategy is to avoid landing on dark blue and then acquire Virginia Avenue to complete the pink set.

Building houses on the pink set would cost only $100 each. I am also considering Mediterranean Avenue for the brown set as a cheap, low-rent option.

The pink set is St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue. Virginia is unowned. Three houses on each property would yield roughly $1400 in total rent if someone lands there.

I cannot build the pink set yet because Virginia Avenue is unowned. I will end my turn unless a trade is offered immediately. Player 1 has only $137 and might be willing to sell Marvin Gardens.

I should not trade for Marvin Gardens. Player 4 already has $869 and a light blue monopoly, so they could build houses immediately and become another lethal threat. Three houses on the light blue set would cost roughly $450 and yield about $270 to $300 in rent per turn, which is survivable with my current cash.

Player 4 could build light blue hotels for roughly $750 total, which I can survive. A yellow monopoly would be more dangerous, but that is secondary to the dark blue threat. I will not trade for Marvin Gardens. I am now considering whether trading with Player 2 could break their dark blue monopoly.

Player 2 would never trade away a dark blue property for money I cannot afford to pay. Indiana Avenue is mortgaged and part of a red set with Player 1, so it would not help me complete a monopoly. I have no valuable assets to offer Player 1 in return.

Player 2 can afford to buy one more house on dark blue without my help, which would raise rent to $1300 or $1700. I will not give them cash. Player 4 has no useful assets to trade for Virginia. I am now considering whether to propose a trade that could acquire Virginia Avenue.

Player 1 is cash-poor. If they go bankrupt, Player 2 or Player 4 could consolidate their assets and become more dangerous. I cannot prevent this this turn. I will end my turn.
